name: Krabi International Airport
before:
The airport for Krabi and the Andaman coast, about 7 km east of the town. It opened in 1999 and is sixth busiest in Thailand, handling 2.3 million passengers in 2023 and over 4.3 million in 2017.

Capacity is the issue to know about. The terminal was designed for three million passengers and passed that some time ago. Money was allocated in 2018 for a third terminal, a refit of the existing two, more aircraft stands and better electrical supply, and a 2019 project aims to double capacity to eight million a year.

After that there is nowhere to go. The airport cannot be expanded beyond its final phase because the town has grown around it, and a new international airport has been proposed in Phang Nga province as the long term alternative.

That electrical work matters more than it sounds. In February 2016 a planned power cut left the terminal dark for over six hours because the back-up generators failed, and immigration staff had to record 2,000 passengers by hand.
after:
The airport for Krabi and the Andaman coast, east of the town.

A third terminal and a refit of the first two have doubled its capacity to eight million passengers a year.

claims.claim: A third terminal and a refit of the first two have doubled its capacity to eight million passengers a year
claims.inAfter: A third terminal and a refit of the first two have doubled its capacity to eight million passengers a year.
claims.note: Replaces the old capacity paragraph, which described the works as money allocated in 2018 and a 2019 project that 'aims to double capacity to eight million a year'. The works are done. On 18 March 2021 Department of Airports officials told Krungthep Turakij that the third terminal, with the refit of terminals 1 and 2 and a car park building (2,923.4 million baht), would raise capacity from 4 million to 8 million passengers a year (1,500 to 3,000 an hour). Krungthep Turakij then reported that the new building would open to passengers on 8 March 2023, with every airline checking in there (one organisation, so the date is not in the text). On 6 August 2026 the department's director-general told Thai Rath the terminal now handles 3,000 passengers an hour, or 8 million a year. Wikipedia describes the same project (a third terminal and a renovation of the existing two, doubling capacity to eight million).

claims.claim: Held back: the Department of Airports still runs Krabi; the transfer to Airports of Thailand is on hold
claims.why: Held back: the old text does not name the operator, so this replaces nothing, but it answers the question of who runs Krabi. The Department of Airports runs it: its own report for the 2025 fiscal year lists Krabi's works among its airports, and news through May 2026 says so. The cabinet agreed in principle on 30 August 2022 to hand the management of Krabi, Udon Thani and Buriram to Airports of Thailand (AOT). The deputy transport minister shelved that in March 2025 (Thai Rath, 6 March 2025; Krabi was the department's most profitable airport, 180 million baht), another deputy minister, Mallika Jirapanvanich, ordered it slowed again (Thansettakij; that page shows no date of its own), and on 7 May 2026 the deputy minister said the handover still stands on the old cabinet resolution but waits for a study, and that he personally opposes it (Thansettakij). Earlier still, the transport ministry kept Krabi with the department while letting AOT manage Udon Thani, Tak and Buriram under contract (Krungthep Turakij, dated 27 August; the year is not on the saved page). So Krabi has not changed hands, whatever the plans. Wikipedia's infobox also says Department of Airports.

claims.claim: Held back: FCDO advice for Thailand
claims.why: Held back: a warning that replaces nothing. The FCDO advises against all but essential travel to the provinces by the Malaysian border (Pattani, Yala, Narathiwat and parts of Songkhla) and within 20 km of the Cambodian border (updated 18 September 2026, still current 24 September 2026). Krabi is in neither area. The page also warns that it is illegal to carry cannabis out of Thailand and that airports scan transiting passengers' bags.
